'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war]]
***[[Humanitarian aid]] deliveries begin arriving at the [[U.S.]]-built [[Gaza floating pier]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/aid-trucks-begin-moving-ashore-via-gaza-pier-us-says-2024-05-17/ (Reuters)]
**[[Rafah offensive]]
***The [[IDF]] retrieves three hostages, having been found deceased. The three were abducted from the [[Nova music festival massacre|Re'im music festival massacre]], including [[Shani Louk]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/live/2024/05/17/world/israel-gaza-war-hamas-rafah (''The New York Times'')]
**[[Hamas]] announces that an [[Israel]]i strike killed Sharhabil Sayed, a Hamas commander in [[Lebanon]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20240517-hamas-says-commander-killed-in-israel-strike-in-lebanon (France 24)]
**Israel announces that an [[Israeli Air Force|Air Force]] strike killed Islaam Hamaisa, a commander of the [[Palestinian Islamic Jihad]]'s [[Jenin Brigades|Jenin Brigade]]. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/article-801603 (''Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[Ukraine]] launches a massive [[Drone warfare|drone attack]] across southwestern [[Russia]], causing fires at several [[Oil refinery|oil refineries]], including at the port of [[Novorossiysk]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/17/world/europe/sevastopol-ukraine-crimea-russia.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[Kharkiv strikes (2022–present)|Kharkiv strikes]]
***At least three [[civilian]]s are killed and 28 others are injured by Russian [[guided bombs]] in [[Kharkiv]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-guided-bombs-kill-two-injure-13-ukraines-kharkiv-2024-05-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[2024 Bamyan shooting]]
**Gunmen open fire on a group of tourists in [[Bamyan Province]], [[Afghanistan]], killing three [[Spain|Spanish]] citizens, two Afghan civilians and a [[Taliban]] guard. Seven others are injured. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/5/18/three-afghans-three-spanish-tourists-killed-in-bamyan-shooting/ (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2024 Ulu Tiram police station attack]]
**Two police officers are killed and another is injured outside the [[Ulu Tiram]] police station in [[Johor]], [[Malaysia]]. The killer is later fatally shot. Seven suspected members of [[Jemaah Islamiyah]] are arrested in connection to the attack. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/malaysia-johor-police-officers-killed-attack-jemaah-islamiyah-4343051 (CNA)]
*[[Hezbollah–Israel conflict]]
**Israeli air strikes kill five people in [[Lebanon]], including two children. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-strikes-kill-least-5-lebanon-including-civilians-2024-05-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[Red Sea crisis]]
**[[Houthi movement|Houthi]] forces shoot down a [[United States Air Force]] [[General Atomics MQ-9 Reaper|MQ-9 Reaper]] drone with a [[surface-to-air missile]] over [[Marib Governorate]], [[Yemen]]. Wreckage of the downed drone appears on [[social media]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/yemens-houthi-rebels-claim-shooting-us-mq-9-110330887 (ABC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*A child in [[Hamilton, Ontario|Hamilton]], [[Ontario]], [[Canada]], dies of [[measles]], the province's first such death since 1989. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/hamilton/measles-death-child-ontario-1.7207293 (CBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Azerbaijan–France relations]], [[2024 New Caledonia unrest]]
**[[France]] accuses [[Azerbaijan]] of being behind the protests and violence in [[New Caledonia]] after Azerbaijani and [[Togo]]lese flags are seen alongside indigenous [[Kanak]] symbols at the protests. Azerbaijan has previously spoken out against [[French colonial empire|French colonialism]] and supported pro-[[New Caledonian independence referendum|independence]] participants, in response to French support for [[Armenia]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/5/17/france-blames-azerbaijan-for-new-caledonia-violence-unpacking-their-spat (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*A man is shot dead by police after trying to set a [[Rouen Synagogue|synagogue]] on fire in [[Rouen]], [[France]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cp3g8kl8dd5o (BBC News)]
*The [[RCMP]] identifies the killer of four people in [[Calgary]], [[Alberta]], [[Canada]], in 1976 and 1977 as [[U.S.|American]] serial rapist [[Gary Allen Srery]], who died in prison in 2011. [https://calgary.ctvnews.ca/serial-sexual-offender-linked-to-unsolved-1970s-homicides-of-four-calgary-girls-women-1.6891238 (CFCN-TV)]
*[[Law Enforcement Command of the Islamic Republic of Iran|Iranian police]] arrest more than 260 people, including three [[Europe|European]] citizens, on suspicion of spreading [[Satanism]] and nudity in [[Iran]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/iran-arrests-260-people-including-3-european-citizens-110343684 (ABC News)]
*Police in [[Louisville]], [[Kentucky]], [[United States]], arrest American golfer [[Scottie Scheffler]], who was travelling to the [[2024 PGA Championship]], for assault of a police officer, criminal [[mischief]], [[reckless driving]], and disregarding traffic signals. [https://apnews.com/article/scheffler-pga-police-fatality-a421bfdb346f00dec95c95a0ab04e4d9 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*A [[Legislative violence#Taiwan|brawl]] breaks out in the [[Legislative Yuan]], [[Taiwan]]'s parliament, following disagreements over draft reforms between the [[Democratic Progressive Party]] and the [[Kuomintang]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/east-asia/taiwan-parliament-fight-reforms-vote-b2546818.html (''The Independent'')]
'''Science and technology'''
*Scientists using the [[James Webb Space Telescope]] discover the earliest known merging of [[black hole]]s, 740 million years after the [[Big Bang]]. [https://apnews.com/article/black-holes-merger-webb-space-telescope-cd5a78e8dfab531f2fa2454d73ad2885 (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*The annual [[FIFA]] Congress in [[Bangkok]], [[Thailand]], awards [[Brazil]] the host rights for the [[2027 FIFA Women's World Cup|2027 Women's World Cup]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2024/05/17/2027-fifa-womens-world-cup-host-brazil/73733595007/ (''USA Today'')]
